ledger.note: 15 August 1310: the Knights Hospitaller take Rhodes. 'On 15 August 1310, after over four years of campaigning, the city of Rhodes surrendered to the knights'; the fleet had sailed from Brindisi in September 1308, and the Knights page adds that they 'gained control of a number of neighbouring islands' around 1310. The year and the city are the page's; the islands are not named, so the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Smyrna, whose defence the knights took over in 1374

ledger.note: 1374: the Knights take over Smyrna. 'In 1374, the Knights took over the defence of Smyrna, conquered by a crusade in 1344.' The Knights Hospitaller page says the same and notes it does not say they held Smyrna from 1344.

ledger.note: 1402: Timur takes Smyrna. 'They held it until it was besieged and taken by Timur in 1402.'

region.text: the stronghold on the peninsula of Halicarnassus (Bodrum) created in 1402

ledger.note: 1402: the Knights build their mainland stronghold at Bodrum. 'In 1402, they created a stronghold on the peninsula of Halicarnassus.' The page names no previous holder; the Menteshe beylik is the researcher's reading of who held Caria in 1402 (Cliopatria's Beylik of Menteshe runs 1305-1414).
1404: the Hospitallers buy Salona. 'Despot Theodore I Palaiologos sold Salona to the Knights Hospitaller in 1404' (Lordship of Salona page).
1410: Salona falls to the Ottomans. The page: 'it fell again to the Ottomans in 1410'.

ledger.note: 26 June 1522: the Ottoman fleet arrives. 'When the Turkish invasion force of 400 ships arrived on Rhodes on 26 June 1522'; Suleiman arrived on 28 July.

ledger.note: 22 December 1522: Rhodes capitulates. 'On 22 December, the representatives of the city's Latin and Greek inhabitants accepted Suleiman's terms'; the knights had twelve days to leave and 'On 1 January 1523, the remaining knights and soldiers marched out of the town'.

wars.name: Hospitaller conquest of Rhodes

zones.text: the island and city of Rhodes, which surrendered to the knights on 15 August 1310

wars.outcome: After over four years of campaigning the city of Rhodes surrendered to the knights on 15 August 1310.
wars.note: The page does not date the landing; 1306 is the researcher's count back from 'over four years' of campaigning, and the page gives September 1308 for the fleet from Brindisi.

wars.name: Defeat of Andronikos III by the Knights of Rhodes
wars.outcome: 'In 1334, the Knights of Rhodes defeated Andronikos III Palaiologos and his Turkish auxiliaries.' The page names no place and no territorial result.

wars.name: Mamluk invasion of Rhodes
wars.outcome: The Knights withstood an invasion by Sultan Sayf ad-Din Jaqmaq in 1444.
wars.note: The Dodecanese page: the fortifications repelled the 'Sultan of Egypt in 1444'.

wars.name: Siege of Rhodes (1480)
wars.outcome: Mehmed II's attack of 1480 'made the Knights a priority target'; the fortifications repelled it (Dodecanese page).
wars.note: The Hospitaller Rhodes and Knights pages give the year and no months.

wars.name: Siege of Rhodes (1522)

union.text: the island and city of Rhodes, which surrendered to the knights on 15 August 1310

wars.outcome: The siege began on 26 June 1522 and lasted six months; the city capitulated on 22 December and the knights marched out on 1 January 1523. The Order moved to Crete and then Sicily.

certainty.note: The Order held islands and harbour towns, whose coasts are the border; the mainland strongholds of Smyrna (1374-1402) and Bodrum (1402-1522) are points with no hinterland on any page, and the extent of the Order's other islands is approximate (page silent on each).

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row for the Hospitaller period (its Domain of Rhodes is 1206-1249, eu-05-c); slug hospitaller-rhodes is the one eu-05-f's Arta dossier already uses as a counterpart. Five pages opened (the Lordship of Salona page supplies the Salona holding of 1404-1410). Not settled: (1) the acquisition dates and list of the Order's islands (Kos, Leros, Kalymnos, Symi, Tilos, Nisyros, Chalki, Kastellorizo): all three pages that mention them are silent, so the Dodecanese region is an upper bound and may include islands the Order never held; (2) who held Rhodes before the Order in 1306-1310 (Byzantine, Genoese under Vignolo de' Vignoli, Menteshe) is not on the pages; (3) Bodrum's previous holder; (4) the grand masters' list (only Foulques de Villaret 1310-1319 and Philippe Villiers de L'Isle-Adam 1521-1522 are named), so no ruler strip; (5) the Knights' 1344-1374 role at Smyrna ('crusade of 1344') needs the Smyrniote crusade page. The Order's later states (Malta from 1530, Tripoli 1530-1551) are separate dossiers (hospitaller-tripoli exists; a Malta dossier belongs to eu-13 or af-02).
